reading.body:
Nebius is building a 300 MW AI factory in Birmingham, Alabama, with first-phase delivery targeted 2028, but the figure comes from city proceedings rather than company publications and a residents' lawsuit over regulatory approval remains pending.

The facility sits on 75 to 80 acres acquired for approximately 90 million dollars and models its design on Nebius's existing 75 MW operation in Finland. At the typical planning density of 1 MW per rack, 300 MW would represent roughly 300 racks of AI compute infrastructure at full buildout, though actual density will depend on final design choices. The site will draw power from Alabama Power.

The regulatory path has been contested. Birmingham's city attorney ruled in April 2026 that the switching station and substation required no city approval, but residents filed a class action lawsuit in May 2026 naming Nebius, the general contractor, the city, and associated entities, later amended to suggest the city may have helped circumvent a data center moratorium. These proceedings remain open and could delay the 2028 timeline or add cost.

This facility is one of only two in Alabama with published capacity figures, making it rare in the state for technical specifications to be available. The build-out depends on resolving the legal challenge and successfully interconnecting to the grid, both binding constraints on compute infrastructure that cannot scale without them.
